page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.16xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The instance is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong performance in memory-intensive and multi-threaded decompression tasks. Specifically, the instance achieves a strong rating in large-block read-only memory bandwidth at 209.21 GB/sec and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 269.5 GB/sec. Passmark CPU extended instructions and database operations also rank in the top 25% tier. Conversely, the server exhibits average performance in standard single-core and multi-core computational tasks, such as stress-ng and Geekbench suites, and shows weak performance in LLM text generation tasks, where the medium 7B model generates 8.69 tokens per second.

Given its high-frequency dedicated CPU cores and 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ecs.hfc6.16xlarge offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local NVMe storage. The strong database operations benchmark makes it appropriate for relational database hosting, multi-threaded data decompression, high-throughput web serving, and parallel compilation tasks. However, the lack of local storage and weak LLM text generation speeds make it less suitable for large-scale AI inference or storage-intensive IOPS-heavy applications.
